question: How many hectares of active wildfires will Russia's Avialesookhrana report in its national bulletin for 00:00 MSK on October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Anchor: the Oct-1 bulletin total has landed in the low thousands in 4 of the last 5 years (median 1,388 ha), with one 77,670 ha outlier driven by a Zabaykalsky autumn complex. The process is strongly mean-reverting at this date - 2021 fell from 90,077 ha on Sep 20 to 636 ha on Oct 1 - so the current 6,680 ha is only a weak predictor of the level 10 days out. Upward pull: the YNAO complex (23 fires / 5,029 ha of the national 6,680) is actively growing under prolonged drought, remote terrain forces manual suppression, and the national total has ticked up every day since Sep 16. Downward pull: Nadym cools to ~0C nights by Sep 30, YNAO's decreed season ended Sep 21, out-of-region crews had already begun rotating home, and Avialesookhrana's October danger outlook points at the South/North Caucasus/Far East rather than the Arctic. I centre modestly above the historical median because a live 5,000 ha complex exists today and the analogue years mostly started near zero. Escape above 60,000 ha needs a Far East or Trans-Baikal autumn blowup from a standing start; that region is running below normal in 2026, but 2024 did exactly this and the 2026 series itself was above 100,000 ha eight days ago - hence 6%. No market exists to cross-check against; evidence is single-instrument (one agency's own bulletin), which argues for keeping the band wide.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the Oct-1 00:00 MSK national active-area figure in the same bulletin series, 2021-2025 = 636 / 3,780 / 1,388 / 77,670 / 509 ha (median 1,388, geometric mean ~2,650, log-SD ~2.0). That class alone is 5-orders-wide and its Oct-1 level is only weakly predicted by the Sep-20 level, because two opposing mechanisms operate over these 11 days: northern/Siberian fires get snuffed by Arctic autumn (2021: 90,077 on Sep 20 -> 636 on Oct 1) while the Far East / Trans-Baikal autumn season opens (2023: 17 -> 1,388; 2025: 2 -> 509; 2024 held 79,953 -> 77,670 on Zabaykalye). Conditioning on 2026: the level has sat at 5,800-6,700 ha for five straight days and is dominated by a re-ignited Yamalo-Nenets event (~5,000-5,400 ha of the total) that Yamal media on Sep 20 described as growing, with 45 natural-fire centres, emergency regime in two districts, remote manual-only suppression, and no precipitation in the Nadym 10-day forecast. That argues the current level does not simply evaporate. Against that: all Yamal fires were fully liquidated on Sep 7 after a single rain episode, so the whole bloc can go to near zero in days; 66-68N in late September strongly favours extinguishment; and 2026 is a below-average year overall (GWIS ~7.5 Mha, ~48% under the two-decade mean). I therefore centre modestly below the current level, with a long right tail: Avialesookhrana's own autumn outlook flags Zabaykalsky and Primorsky Krai above the multi-year norm and Primorye's autumn season opened Sep 17, which is exactly the 2024 mechanism that produced a 77,670 ha reading. I priced 5% above the 60,000 ha open upper bound - lower than the naive 1-in-5 class rate because, unlike Sep 19 2024 when Zabaykalye already held 76,564 ha, no comparable bloc is burning anywhere today and an Arctic ramp to 60,000+ in 11 days is not physically plausible in late September. Market check: the harness found no Polymarket or Manifold candidate; my own search of Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/Metaculus and bookmakers found no contract on Russian wildfire hectares at all (only US-focused wildfire contracts) - no market anchor exists, so nothing was blended.

calls.reference_class: Avialesookhrana national active forest-fire area ('площадь, пройденная огнём') reported in the 00:00 MSK bulletin dated October 1, years 2021-2025

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Avialesookhrana's Oct-1 00:00 MSK national active-fire area, 2021-2025 = 509/636/1388/3780/77670 ha, median 1388. Two adjustments push above that median. First, the current level is unusually high for the date: 6,360 ha on Sep 19 versus 2 ha (2025) and 17 ha (2023) on Sep 20, and it has risen, not fallen, over Sep 15-19 despite 888-1380 personnel. Second, ~75-84% of it is a Yamalo-Nenets smouldering moss/duff complex that manual crews have failed to shrink for five days. Pushing down: YNAO is a 65-66 degN Arctic region whose season reliably hard-stops on snow and frost within the 12-day horizon, and it was declared fully liquidated once already on Sep 7 before re-igniting; Yakutia's giants are gone and the under-observation inventory has drained from 620,606 to 11,219 ha, removing the reclassification channel that generated September's huge prints; and 2026 nationally is ~48% below the two-decade average. The upside tail is real but not currently loaded: the 2024 Oct-1 print of 77,670 ha was a Transbaikal regime already burning 81,137 ha on Sep 10, whereas today's Far East contribution is one 350 ha Primorye fire at the start of its autumn season. I price 5% above the 60,000 ha upper bound on a Transbaikal/Amur/Primorye autumn outbreak or a large Far East complex re-entering the actively-suppressed column. Distribution is strongly right-skewed on a log scale; no market exists to anchor against.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the same bulletin's Oct-1 figure 2021-2025 = 636/3780/1388/77670/509 ha, median ~1388, geometric mean ~2660. Status quo is 6,360 ha (30 fires) on 2026-09-19, but ~80% of that is Yamalo-Nenets AO, where forecasts call for end-of-September frost, rain and wet snow and where 7 of the fires are already localized; the 2021 analogue (88,840 ha of Arctic Yakutia fires on Sep 18 collapsing to 636 ha by Oct 1) argues the residual fades hard. Pulling the other way: Avialesookhrana's October outlook flags elevated risk in the Southern, North Caucasus and Far Eastern districts, Primorye's autumn season opened 2026-09-15 with its Terney fire already at 350 ha and growing, 43 regions remain under special fire regime, and in 2 of 4 clean past transitions the Oct-1 figure rose above the mid-September level (2022 1,032->3,780; 2023 93->1,388). So I sit modestly above the class median. The upside escape is real but weaker than the 1-in-5 raw base rate: the only >60,000 ha Oct-1 in the class (2024, 98% Zabaikalsky Krai) was already at ~80,000 ha nationally on Sep 19 of that year, whereas Zabaikalye, Amur and Buryatia have zero active fires today and Zabaikalye's 2026 burned area is reported down - hence 6%, not 20%. A further cap: this year Avialesookhrana has been aggressively reclassifying large remote fires as 'under observation' (620,606 ha so excluded on Sep 13), which structurally suppresses the counted opening-sentence total. No market prices this contract.

calls.reasoning: Class median is 1,388 ha with one 77,670 ha outlier (2024, 98% Zabaykalsky, already at ~80,000 ha twelve days prior). The 20.09.2026 status quo is 6,680 ha / 35 fires, rising since 16.09 and ~80% Yamalo-Nenets. The headline figure is cumulative area per fire, so it leaves the total only on liquidation or reclassification: the Yamal bloc persists until crews or weather kill fires individually, and the 07.09 full liquidation after one rain shows the wholesale exit channel is fast. At 65-66N with daytime highs near 4C and sub-zero nights by 30.09, spread stops; whether the bloc is cleared turns on precipitation, which no run could establish. Hence a bimodal-leaning mixture centred modestly above the class median. Upside is real but unloaded - Zabaykalye/Amur/Buryatia at zero, 2026 ~48% below the two-decade mean - so 4% above 60,000 ha, against a naive 1-in-5 class rate. No prediction market exists on this quantity.
calls.reconciliation: Settled the status quo at 6,680 ha (20.09 bulletin): Runs 1 and 2 retrieved it independently with a regional breakdown that sums exactly, while Runs 3 and 4 were simply reading a lagging relay. Settled YNAO's direction toward growth: the 'crews withdrawing' report Run 4 leans on is the pre-reburn early-September rotation that Run 1's own timeline places before the 10.09 re-ignition, whereas reinforcement, re-imposed emergency regimes and a rising centre count on 20.09 are corroborated by two runs. Could not settle the Nadym precipitation forecast - one low-confidence 10-day showing ~0 mm against media reports of an end-September cold wave with wet snow - so that uncertainty is carried as the branch weight rather than resolved by fiat. I adopted the runs' shared reference class and their reading of the resolution instrument (opening sentence includes other-category and protected-area lines, excludes 'под наблюдением'), which all four verified arithmetically. My median sits above Runs 3 and 4 because the metric does not decay smoothly - a live 5,400 ha Yamal complex keeps counting until its fires are individually liquidated - and below Run 2 because that persistence has no growth engine left at 65N in late September. I cut the upper escape to 4% on the observation that every past >60,000 ha Oct-1 print had its bloc already visible mid-September, and none is visible now.
